## Recursive rules · Fibonacci {#ss1-recursive-rules}

A recursive definition needs **starting values** and a rule using earlier terms.

For the familiar Fibonacci sequence:

$$a_1=1,\qquad a_2=1,\qquad a_n=a_{n-1}+a_{n-2}\quad(n\ge3).$$

<div data-module="fibonacci" class="fibonacci-builder" aria-label="Build the Fibonacci sequence one term at a time"></div>

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 1 · Recursive rules · Next: Example 1.5</p>

::: notes
This is the familiar sequence 1,1,2,3,5,8,…, while the staircase counts began 1,2,3,5,8,… . Both obey the same recurrence, but their starting values differ.

Use Next term to reveal a term only after a prediction. The two terms used are highlighted and the calculation is displayed. Two or three reveals are sufficient. Reset restores only the starting values. Ask why both starting values are needed and what a_{n-1} and a_{n-2} mean.

In Example 1.5 only the immediately preceding term is used, with a multiplier depending on n. Source: https://oeis.org/A000045.
:::
